milestone: Brownie MCP Runtime Safety Policy Finite Closure

strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Keeps MCP tool execution success evidence owned by Runtime status semantics instead of server prose or result text.
Prevents autonomous loops from treating MCP tool-side errors as successful context, verification evidence, or completed-success replay.
Preserves bounded tool execution and ledger evidence behavior while leaving workspace, Git, verifier, and completion tools inside the Runtime.

answers.new_capability: Brownie now conforms the Runtime MCP tools/call boundary to current CallToolResult semantics: resultType complete is normal, omitted resultType is backward-compatible complete, input_required fails closed in v0, omitted isError defaults to false, and malformed content/isError remain bounded failures.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: MCP-S1 separated protocol success from tool success, but still required explicit isError=false and did not parse current resultType semantics, so protocol-conformant servers that omit isError could fail incorrectly and input_required results were not explicitly rejected.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: A protocol-conformant MCP server could be misclassified, while unsupported input_required continuations would lack an explicit fail-closed Runtime status before later MCP safety policy phases compose around this boundary.
answers.non_duplicative: This phase changes controlled MCP execution classification and tests the ledger/replay boundary; it does not add another audit-only report, endpoint, adapter, or wrapper.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. The existing tool.execute, task.run, and headless run/resume paths are preserved.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The phase adds bounded execution status metadata to existing MCP tool-result payloads and a campaign audit artifact, not a new user-facing summary API.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Explicit isError=true still emits ToolExecutionFailed with bounded MCP context; explicit isError=false or omitted isError can emit ToolExecutionCompleted only for complete results, while input_required and unknown resultType values are not completed-success replay evidence.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Headless autonomous runs can accept current MCP complete results without false failure while still failing closed for unsupported multi-round-trip input semantics.
answers.milestone_progress: Corrects MCP-S1 to the current MCP protocol baseline before MCP-S2 starts, without broadening MCP transport, approval, schema, secret, annotation, or executable-identity scope.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: MCP-S1.1 updates the phase-value manifest and MCP Runtime Safety audit registration, so strict review must verify that protocol conformance cannot mask open Runtime release blockers or convert excluded MCP transport/product work into this P0 phase.

exit_criteria: MCP tools/call result classification treats explicit isError=false and omitted isError as ToolSucceeded only for complete results.
Explicit isError=true records ToolExecutionFailed with bounded MCP context and policy-controlled retry metadata.
resultType complete and absent backward-compatible resultType are accepted; input_required and unknown resultType values fail closed.
JSON-RPC error, timeout, input_required, unknown resultType, and malformed result paths are distinct bounded failure statuses.
MCP tool error evidence is not used as second-pass prompt/completion evidence and is not replayed as a completed success.
MCP Runtime Safety Policy audit classifies MCP-S1 through MCP-S7 without replacing the MCP-first architecture.
behavior_evidence: cargo test -p brownie-runtime mcp -- --test-threads=1 covers successful MCP calls, omitted isError success, isError=true tool errors, JSON-RPC protocol failure, timeout, input_required fail-closed handling, unknown resultType protocol failure, malformed result failure, bounded result context, and completed-success replay.
docs/specifications/mcp-client-spec-v0.md and docs/specifications/tool-execution-spec-v0.md define the S1 result semantics.
docs/architecture/mcp-runtime-safety-policy-audit.json records S1 closed and S2-S7 remaining required-before-release Runtime debt.

accepted_capability: Runtime MCP tools/call success evidence is now restricted to complete results with explicit isError=false or omitted isError.
Runtime MCP tool-side errors now produce bounded failure evidence instead of completed-success replay evidence.
behavior_evidence: Focused MCP runtime tests cover isError=false success, omitted isError success, isError=true tool failure, JSON-RPC protocol failure, timeout, input_required fail-closed handling, unknown resultType protocol failure, malformed result failure, bounded context, and success replay preservation.
Agent-loop MCP test coverage proves ToolReturnedError does not create SecondPassPromptBuilt or ToolExecutionCompleted MCP evidence.
safety_boundary: Rust Runtime remains the permission, execution, ledger, replay, and completion authority for MCP calls.
MCP server description, schema, annotation, result text, AgentModes prose, CLI, VSIX, and LLM output cannot grant authority.

Failure payloads retain bounded metadata and do not ledger raw JSON-RPC responses, raw errors, secrets, environment values, absolute paths, canonical paths, prompts, provider responses, or binary content.
non_goals: Does not add a Brownie-specific tool adapter SDK or protocol.

Does not add Streamable HTTP, OAuth, MCP Apps, Sampling, Roots, Elicitation, public registry, automatic install, scheduler, daemon, generic shell, arbitrary process execution, or recursive Brownie invocation.
Does not close MCP-S2 through MCP-S7.
rejected_alternatives: Rejected expanding the external ToolExecuteStatus enum before a broader protocol contract review.
Rejected treating input_required as an implicit prompt continuation because v0 does not implement MCP multi-round-trip input, Elicitation, Roots, Sampling, or remote transport behavior.
Rejected using MCP tool error text as completion or verification evidence.

MCP external mutation/destructive call approval binding remains open.
Runtime still needs bounded input/output schema validation for MCP tools/call.
